title: Finite covers of projective schemes are projective
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $p:T\to S$ be projective in the global closed-embedding convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism], and let $h:Y\to T$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $p\circ h$ is locally projective in the following explicit sense: for every affine open $U\subseteq S$, with $T_U=p^{-1}(U)$ and $Y_U=(p\circ h)^{-1}(U)$, there exist $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $Y_U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_U$ over $U$. Thus $Y_U\to U$ is projective in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. In particular, if $S$ is affine, $Y\to S$ is projective. No global projective-space embedding is asserted when $S$ is arbitrary.

proof.text: For an affine base, extract the finite coordinate type n and the closed immersion T into projective space from [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Apply the existing, proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.ProjectiveSpace.exists_isClosedImmersion_of_isFinite to that immersion and the finite map h [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This theorem already implements the coordinate-section argument of this node: the twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist] has coordinate sections whose nonvanishing loci are the standard affine charts; inverse images under the finite map followed by the closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] are affine and cover Y. The native ample-family immersion theorem applies using finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The composite is proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper], [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], with properness as in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Projective space is separated [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated], so the immersion is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed]. The source theorem returns a closed immersion into projective space indexed by an arbitrary finite type m.

Normalize the finite coordinate type to ULift (Fin (N+1)) using [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-finite-index-iso] when m is nonempty. Compose the closed immersion with the supplied isomorphism over the base. If m is empty then its projective space is empty by its standard-chart cover [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], so Y is empty; its unique map into projective zero-space is a closed immersion and is over the base. In either case [def-pc-projective-morphism] gives H-projectivity. Properness of H-projective maps [lem-pc-projective-proper] gives quasi-compactness, hence projectivity.

proof.text: For each affine open U of S, restrict the closed immersion of T into projective space using the cartesian square for projective-space base change [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Closed immersions are preserved under this base change [def-weil-closed-immersion], giving H-projectivity of the restricted map [def-pc-projective-morphism]. The restriction of h is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply the affine-base result and use morphismRestrict_comp to identify the composite with the restriction of h followed by p. This proves the explicit local embedding and local projectivity. When S itself is affine, apply the same affine-base result directly.
